mainEntity.name: How much does an Audi A3 40 TDI Quattro engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: The cost to replace an Audi A3 40 TDI Quattro engine typically ranges from £1,200 for a used unit to £3,800-£6,000 for a fully rebuilt engine (supply-only). Adding specialist supply & fit labour will generally increase the total by £520-£715, depending on the workshop's location and the specific engine code (DJGA or DTUA).

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of a failing engine in an Audi A3 40 TDI Quattro?

acceptedAnswer.text: Owners of the Audi A3 40 TDI Quattro should watch for persistent engine management lights, excessive blue or black smoke from the exhaust, and a noticeable loss of power or limp mode.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in an Audi A3 40 TDI Quattro?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, for most owners, it is financially viable. The Audi A3 40 TDI Quattro retains strong residual values, typically ranging from £12,000 to £28,000 depending on the year and condition. A rebuilt engine is a sensible investment for an 8Y (2020+) model.

mainEntity.name: How long does an Audi A3 40 TDI Quattro engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A professional supply and fit engine replacement for an Audi A3 40 TDI Quattro typically takes 2 to 3 working days, including vehicle intake, engine removal, installation, ECU coding, and comprehensive road testing.

mainEntity.name: Will any 2.0 TDI engine fit my Audi A3 40 TDI Quattro?

acceptedAnswer.text: No, you must ensure the replacement engine matches your specific engine code (e.g., DJGA, DGCA, or DTUA) and is configured for Quattro all-wheel drive. Non-Quattro engines lack the necessary rear differential drive components and mounting points.

historyTimeline.h2: Audi A3 40 TDI Quattro - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: Launched as the premium diesel performance variant of the A3 range, the 40 TDI Quattro badge signifies a 2.0-litre turbocharged diesel with all-wheel drive, evolving through the 8V facelift and into the modern 8Y generation with refined efficiency and increased power outputs.

milestones.description: DJGA / DGCA, 2.0L TDI, 184hp (135kW). Introduced with the 8V facelift, replacing older numerical badging with the new "40 TDI" nomenclature, paired with a 7-speed S tronic and Quattro all-wheel drive.

DTUA, 2.0L TDI, 200hp (147kW). Launched with the all-new 8Y generation, featuring updated EA288 Evo architecture, mild-hybrid assistance in some markets, and increased power output while maintaining Quattro traction.

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every engine fitted to the Audi A3 40 TDI Quattro is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points.

commonProblems.h2: Audi A3 40 TDI Quattro Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The Audi A3 40 TDI Quattro is generally robust, with the EA288 2.0 TDI family proving significantly more reliable than its EA189 predecessor. However, emissions control components and high-mileage wear can lead to costly repairs. Rebuilt engines through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: AdBlue & EGR System Failures - Why the Audi A3 40 TDI Quattro (DJGA/DTUA) Triggers Warning Lights
problems.affectedModels: Audi A3 40 TDI Quattro (DJGA, DGCA, DTUA, 2018-present)
problems.rootCause: The AdBlue heater element or NOx sensors can fail, while the EGR cooler is susceptible to internal leaks, triggering engine management lights and potential limp mode.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replacement of faulty NOx sensor, AdBlue heater, or EGR cooler flush/replace.
repairOptions.longevity: Viable if the core engine block and turbo are healthy.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit of reconditioned/rebuilt EA288 2.0 TDI, upgraded components, 12-month warranty.
repairOptions.longevity: The right call if multiple emissions components fail alongside high-mileage wear.

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical 2018-2020 Audi A3 40 TDI Quattro is valued at approximately £12,000-£18,000, while 2020+ 8Y models sit around £18,000-£28,000 [THIRD-PARTY]. For vehicles worth £8,000-£15,000+, a reconditioned or rebuilt replacement comfortably justifies the premium via warranty and reliability, keeping the repair cost well within the vehicle's retained value.
problems.recommendation: For isolated AdBlue or EGR faults on a well-maintained Audi A3 40 TDI Quattro, targeted component repair is the most cost-effective route. However, if the vehicle has exceeded 150k miles and exhibits multiple concurrent issues, a reconditioned engine replacement offers superior long-term value and peace of mind.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt DJGA/DTUA Audi A3 40 TDI Quattro engine prices

problems.h4: DPF Clogging & Turbo Wear - High-Mileage Stress on the Audi A3 40 TDI Quattro
problems.rootCause: Frequent short, urban journeys prevent the diesel particulate filter (DPF) from completing active regeneration cycles, leading to ash buildup and increased backpressure that can prematurely wear the turbocharger.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Off-car DPF cleaning and turbo actuator calibration.
repairOptions.longevity: Suitable only if caught early, before structural turbo damage occurs.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit of reconditioned/rebuilt EA288 2.0 TDI, upgraded components, 12-month warranty.
repairOptions.longevity: Necessary if DPF blockage has caused catastrophic turbo failure or oil starvation.

problems.vehicleValueCheck: As above, the Audi A3 40 TDI Quattro retains strong value. A £4,300-£6,700 specialist rebuilt replacement represents a sensible investment for an 8Y model, whereas an older 8V nearing the end of its lifecycle may warrant a careful cost-benefit analysis against a high-quality used replacement.
problems.recommendation: Preventative motorway driving is the best defence against DPF issues. If turbo failure has already occurred due to DPF-induced oil starvation, replacing the entire unit with a rebuilt engine is safer than attempting a standalone turbo swap, which risks contamination from existing debris.
